title: Issuing a Travel Credit Voucher against a Cancelled Air Ticket Fare Brands Booking
content:
A travel credit voucher raised against a cancelled Air Ticket Fare Brands booking is issued on the conditions below.

## 1. The state condition

A voucher is issued only while the booking record stands at cancelled, refund pending or refunded. The booking record is the authority for that state and is read against this booking's own reference.

## 2. Whose voucher it is

The voucher is issued in the name of the traveller the ticket was issued to, and is transferable only where the producing brand makes credits transferable.

## 3. Reissue of a lapsed voucher

A voucher that has lapsed may be reissued 1 time and no more. Where a brand's credit validity term is zero the brand issues no voucher at all, and its cancelled value is forfeited.

## 4. Value is never paid out in money

The value on a voucher is never paid out in money, not even where the traveller no longer intends to travel.

## 5. Clauses no longer in force

> "A travel credit is issued for the value the cancelled ticket still carried after any penalty has been withheld, and carries an expiry set by the credit validity term of the fare brand that produced it."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the value placed on a travel credit voucher on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

> "A voucher that has lapsed may be reissued once onto a fresh voucher against the brand's reissue fee, and the fresh voucher carries the same validity term counted from the day of reissue."

That clause is **no longer in force**. The handling basis it stated has been superseded by the basis now governing the release of value standing on a travel credit voucher on Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings. The brand values scheduled under this policy are unaffected and stand as stated.

The basis those two clauses carried — the voucher raised for the value the cancelled ticket still carried once any penalty had been withheld, with an expiry taken from the producing brand's credit validity term, and a lapsed voucher reissued against the brand's reissue fee onto a fresh voucher running the same term from the day of reissue — is retired with them. Sections 1 to 4 are unaffected and remain in force, and the credit validity term, reissue fee and transferability scheduled for each brand remain that brand's own values.

## 6. Points of judgement

**Does the retirement touch the limit in section 3?** It does not. The limit of 1 reissue stands as a condition in force; what is retired is the basis on which a reissue was priced and dated.

**A brand whose credit validity term is zero.** No voucher is issued at all under section 3, whatever the value the cancelled ticket carried.

superseded_clauses: A travel credit is issued for the value the cancelled ticket still carried after any penalty has been withheld, and carries an expiry set by the credit validity term of the fare brand that produced it.
A voucher that has lapsed may be reissued once onto a fresh voucher against the brand's reissue fee, and the fresh voucher carries the same validity term counted from the day of reissue.
